Documentation → Automation & Change Control → Triggers

Triggers and automations on a trigger

Make SATOM an orchestrator. A trigger (Automations › Triggers) is a condition on an event — an alert, a change, an automation that finished, a call from an outside system. An automation on a trigger (Automations) is what happens then — a process walk, a Plugin Studio app, a script, an API Catalog call, SQL, a data-store write, a hook, a scheduled action or a notification.

👤 ForAdministratorOperator
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage operations.apply
📍 WhereOperations → Automation → Automations → Triggers tab (URL /administration/triggers/) · Operations → Automation → Automations → On a trigger (URL /web/automations/on-trigger/)

What is it?#

Scheduled actions start on a clock. Triggers start work when something happens, and they come in two halves on purpose:

  • A trigger is the condition — one event, narrowed to the occurrences that matter. Administrators create triggers under Administrator → Change Management → Triggers.
  • An automation on a trigger is the implementation — what SATOM does when the trigger matches. Operators manage them under Automations → On a trigger.

One trigger can feed several automations: a "critical device alert" can walk a diagnostics process, open a ticket through an API and post a chat message, with the filter written once.

What does it do?#

  • Events: alert.fired (every fresh alert finding, whatever the notification channels say), intent.deviation, change.requested, change.approved, window.opening, window.closing, upgrade.finished, upgrade.failed, automation.finished (an automation ended — this is how automations chain) and api.event (an outside system called POST /api/v1/events).
  • Conditions: ADOMs, alert families, minimum severity, appliance ids, alert key glob (device.*), text contained in the title or detail, API event type glob, the finished automation and its outcome, and JSON payload conditions ({"field": "data.priority", "op": "equals", "value": "P1"}).
  • Bounds: a cooldown per subject (the same alert key, change or API subject) and a budget of matches per hour. A refused match is recorded as suppressed with the reason.
  • What an automation can do: run a published Plugin Studio app (a runbook too) (the event is {{ event }} inside it); run a Script Library script; call an HTTP connection — only that version's endpoints when the connection is pinned to an API Catalog version; query a PostgreSQL connection; write a Studio data store; run an integration hook; run an existing scheduled action now; notify by bell and/or e-mail.
  • Rehearsal by default: an automation that is not armed records its writes instead of executing them.
  • Everything is a job and everything is recorded: each match, refusal and run, with a link to the real record (app-run:5, action-run:9, …).

Requirements#

  • A trigger needs users.manage (Administrator). An automation needs config_write (the Automations page's own permission).
  • What an automation runs must exist and be usable: a published app the owner may use, a published script, an existing connection, hook or scheduled action. The form lists every problem before you save.

Permissions#

Action Needs
Create, edit, preview, delete a trigger users.manage
Create, edit, test, delete an automation on a trigger config_write
Bind a System Automation (scheduled action of the system catalog) users.manage
Post an event from outside API token with write scope
List triggers from outside API token with read scope

An automation runs as its owner — the user who saved it last. A Studio app it starts must be one that user may use; a script reads that user's vault entries.

How to use#

  1. Create the trigger. Administrator → Triggers → New trigger. Give it a key (critical-device), choose the event (alert.fired) and narrow it: family device, minimum severity critical. Leave the cooldown at 60 minutes. Preview shows which current alert findings would match.
  2. Bind what it does. On the trigger page click Bind an automation, or go to Automations → On a trigger → New automation. Choose the trigger, then Do: Run a Plugin Studio app → collect-diagnostics, form values {"appliance": "{{ event.appliance_id }}"}. Leave Armed off for a rehearsal.
  3. Test it. On the automation page, Run a rehearsal runs it once with the event's documented example (or a payload you paste). The result is in Runs.
  4. Chain the next step. Create a second trigger on automation.finished with finished automation collect-diagnostics and outcome failed, and bind it to Call an API on your ticketing connection with the body {"title": "{{ event.summary }}"}.

Text fields are templates over the event: {{ event.title }}, {{ event.appliance_id }}, {{ event.data.ticket }}, {{ trigger.key }}. An optional value is {{ x | default('') }}.

Configuration#

Field Meaning Default
Event What the trigger listens to —
Conditions All must hold; empty = any; a condition on a field the event lacks is not met any
Cooldown per subject Minutes before the same subject matches again (0 = always) 60
Matches per hour Budget; past it a match is suppressed (0 = no budget) 20
Do What the automation runs —
Armed Off = rehearsal (writes recorded, not executed) off
Enabled Off = the automation is skipped on

Example#

An outside CI pipeline tells SATOM a deployment finished:

curl -X POST https://satom.example/api/v1/events \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"type": "deploy.done", "subject": "build-42", "appliance_id": 3,
       "data": {"service": "shop"}}'

A trigger on api.event with type deploy.* starts a Plugin Studio app that calls the service's health endpoint through the API Catalog, walks the post-change validation process on appliance 3 and writes the outcome to a data store.

Result#

The call answers 202 with the triggers that matched and the automations queued. The trigger's page lists the match; the automation's page lists the run, its status and where the real record is.

Troubleshooting#

Symptom Why What to do
Match listed as suppressed Cooldown, hourly budget, or a chain deeper than 3 hops Read the reason; lower the cooldown or raise the budget
Run skipped: owner missing or disabled The user who saved it was disabled Save the automation again as an active user
Run skipped: process acts on a device The event names no appliance Give the appliance on the automation (id or name, a template is fine)
API call shows [rehearsal] The automation is not armed Arm it, once the rehearsal shows what you expect
A hook run fails "still queued" The integrations runner did not pick it up Check the integrations runner on the node

Advanced#

  • A chain stops after 3 hops of automation.finished: a trigger that matches its own automation would otherwise loop.
  • A runbook is a Plugin Studio app: one app diagram can check devices, ask a person, call APIs, run scripts and query data. An event starts it through a Run a Plugin Studio app automation; a rehearsal run never writes, an armed run writes only for a user who holds config_write.
  • GET /api/v1/triggers lists triggers and their enabled automations, so a caller can see which event types anything listens to.
